disclaimer: This report is for educational and wellness purposes only. It is not a medical diagnosis and does not replace advice from a qualified healthcare professional. HbA1c results should be confirmed by your doctor. Do not start, stop or change any medication without medical advice.

status.label: In the normal range
status.explanation: Your HbA1c reflects average blood glucose over roughly the last 2–3 months and is below the 5.7% threshold used for prediabetes.

summary: Your HbA1c of 5.3 is in the normal range, which is a great sign that your blood sugar is currently well managed. Your BMI of 22.7 also falls in the normal category, and your very active lifestyle is a strong plus for long-term health. The main risk factor to address is current smoking, which can affect blood vessels, blood pressure, and overall glucose handling over time. Keeping up with routine HbA1c and blood pressure checks, staying active, and working toward reducing or quitting smoking are the most valuable next steps.

foods_to_eat: Whole grains like quinoa, brown rice and oats
Lean proteins such as chicken, turkey, fish and eggs
Legumes including beans, lentils and chickpeas
Plenty of vegetables, especially leafy greens and peppers
Healthy fats from olive oil, nuts, seeds and avocado
Fruits such as berries, apples and citrus
Low-fat dairy like yogurt and cottage cheese
plan.portion_guidance: Fill half your plate with vegetables, a quarter with lean protein and a quarter with whole grains at lunch and dinner. Since your activity level is very high, include a wholesome snack before or after workouts to support recovery and energy needs.
plan.hydration: Aim for about 3 to 3.5 litres of water daily, more on training days, and limit sugary or alcoholic drinks.
based_on: very active lifestyle: higher protein and carbohydrate needs
current smoker: emphasis on nutrient-dense whole foods

exercise: Since you're already very active, keep up at least 150 minutes a week of moderate activity, or continue your higher intensity routine if you're used to it.
Include muscle-strengthening activities on at least 2 days a week, covering major muscle groups.
Mix in variety like cycling, swimming, or sports to keep things enjoyable and sustainable.
lifestyle.walking_goal: Aim for at least 30 minutes of brisk walking on 5 days a week; since you're already very active, you can build this in as extra recovery or active-rest activity, starting with your current habits and adjusting as needed.
lifestyle.weight_management: Your BMI is in the normal range, so the focus should be on maintaining your current healthy weight through balanced eating and regular activity, not on weight loss.
lifestyle.sleep: Try to get 7 to 9 hours of sleep each night. Keep a consistent bedtime and wake time, avoid screens for at least 30 minutes before bed, and keep your bedroom cool and dark.
stress: Practice deep breathing exercises for 5 to 10 minutes a day, especially during busy periods.
Try mindfulness or meditation apps to build a regular relaxation habit.
Make time for hobbies or activities you enjoy to help unwind after work.
behaviour_change: Since you currently smoke, consider taking steps to quit. Calling a quitline, such as a free national smoking cessation helpline, can provide support and a personalised plan.
Talk to your doctor about strategies and support options to help you stop smoking, since quitting has strong benefits for your long-term health.
Continue to keep your alcohol intake occasional, as you currently do, to support overall wellbeing.
Set small, achievable goals for lifestyle changes and track your progress to stay motivated.

monitoring.name: HbA1c
monitoring.why: Regular screening finds changes before symptoms appear.
monitoring.frequency: Every 3 years, or yearly if your doctor advises because of risk factors

monitoring.name: Blood pressure
monitoring.why: High blood pressure multiplies the heart and kidney risks of high blood glucose.
monitoring.frequency: At every doctor visit; at home regularly if you have high blood pressure

preventive_actions: Consider seeking support or resources to reduce or quit smoking, since it can affect blood vessel health and glucose regulation over time
Continue regular physical activity, which helps maintain healthy blood sugar and body weight
Keep your calorie intake near your 2900 target to support your active lifestyle and maintain your current healthy weight
Schedule routine HbA1c checks to continue monitoring your blood sugar trends over time
Monitor your blood pressure regularly, especially given the added strain smoking can place on the cardiovascular system
Limit alcohol intake to occasional moderate amounts to support overall metabolic health

How often should I check my HbA1c and blood pressure given my current lifestyle?

hba1c_caveat: HbA1c can be less accurate if you have anaemia, kidney disease, a recent blood transfusion or certain haemoglobin variants.
